summary: The SDK keys a nested-file child by its host-qualified address too, so two hosts each carrying a `home` child emit instead of colliding on `duplicate identity key`

edit.description: One home for a member's own address: the `<host-address>/<kind>/<key>` form when the member carries a host (a nested-file child), `hostAddress(kind, name)` otherwise — the twin of the engine-side home, so the two sides spell one grammar.

`memberTable` and `nestedTargets` key every projected member through the new home, so a nested-file child enters the table at its host-qualified address (and, like an embedded member, under its bare key when one host carries it) instead of colliding in `uniqueMap` at `kind:name`; the edge-placement and rendered-extent sites that colon-join `member.kind`/`member.name` do the same.

The six sites spelling a member's own address — the satisfies rows, the edge rows, the assembly facts, the nested-member row host, and `declaredAddresses` (what a mention may name) — go through the one home, so a file child is declared, cited and mentioned under the address it actually resolves at.
A mention's resolved target address comes from the one home, so a mention of a file child spells its host-qualified address.
The new home: a hosted member composes the nested form, a top-level one the `kind:name` form.
Two hosts each carrying a same-named file child emit both projections, and each is reachable in the member table at its host-qualified address.
The duplicate-identity refusal still fires where it should — one host carrying the same `(kind, key)` twice — and no longer fires across hosts.
End to end through a real `node` program: a corpus whose two directory-unit hosts each carry a `home` file child emits both files and `check` counts two members of the child kind.

tests.asserts: two hosts, one child name: emit produces both projections and neither collides
the one home composes the nested form for a hosted member and `kind:name` otherwise
the two-host corpus emits and checks clean, counting both children

acceptance: `pnpm --dir sdk test` and `cargo test` green, with the inbox reproduction — a directory-unit host kind templating `{kind: note, path: "*.json"}` over hosts `alpha` and `beta`, one `home` child each — emitting rather than failing `duplicate identity key 'note:home'`.
notes: Routed from the inbox: note 3 (observed at 040e2d1c). The SDK half, serialized behind the engine half so the address the SDK starts writing is one the engine already resolves. Widens a shared enumeration's spelling: every site that colon-joins `member.kind`/`member.name` is a consumer, which is why the one home lands first. scoped at 6184091f
